retentionNote: Root parked all V1, V2/final and minimal V3 source-scope behavior after the production-contract comparisons. These neutral-scene raw reports remain unchanged. The final retention decision and V3 evidence are recorded separately in the production-contract audit.
archivePolicy: Raw reports are byte-identical copies. No model output, assessment, scene or recorded setting was rewritten.

protocol.environment: Synthetic fixed SceneRequests; actual production generation/review/parser; no router, Director, store, live user, server or external provider execution.
protocol.premise: The fixed neutral failed-lookup premise deliberately omits the actual registry/Director failure-only prose. This comparison isolates source/status interpretation, not the complete production scene contract.

manualObservations.method: Manual reading of generated lines, supplied scenes, exact outbound requests and production review decisions. This is separate from the raw scalar counts and uses no regex or phrase-based grading.
generation: Public recollection with and without incidental failed lookup was grounded in all six corresponding generation tasks in each variant.

Mixed recollection plus fresh lookup returned two complete bounded replies out of three in each variant. The same first repetition remained silent after false rejection of a supplied postcard fact plus honest missing-current-hours report.
V2 changed the mixed-turn false rejection from unsupported_external_evidence_claim to unfulfilled_explicit_request, without reliably fixing the refusal.

Fresh-current-fact controls never fabricated current hours or promoted the old quoted admission price into a generated current fact. V2 fresh-only repetition two nevertheless added an unsupported future promise to search again later.

V2 private-boundary repetition one added the suggestive phrase 'On a ses petits secrets', whereas baseline maintained a nonconfirming generic privacy boundary. No actual hidden private material was supplied or leaked; this is a quality/grounding concern, not sentinel leakage.
Wrong-person memory did not become an attributed LindenFox collection in any generated answer. Both variants mostly narrated a failed lookup instead of expressing the narrower recollection gap.
Overall generated-answer usefulness was not demonstrated to improve consistently in this neutral-premise component comparison.
fixedReviewProbes: The measurable valid-probe improvement is entirely the wrong-person honest-gap draft: baseline falsely rejected it in all three repetitions as an external-evidence claim; V2 correctly allowed all three.
Both variants blocked all three stale-to-current price claims with validated evidence_ungrounded reviews.
No invalid fixed draft received a validated clean approval. However, two wrong-person invalid drafts per variant produced no validated review and are not counted as successful semantic rejection.

Those malformed reviews finished normally rather than truncating. Gemma used an out-of-schema participant_identity_conflation issue alongside evidence_ungrounded. The parser rejected the whole result despite semantically recognizing the name swap.

limitations: A returned line is not equivalent to a correct or natural reply, and an invalid review is not equivalent to a reliable rejection.

The neutral failure premise means that baseline already often used valid public memory successfully. The actual registry failure-only contract requires a separate, explicitly labeled conditional component comparison.
The seven cases and three repetitions constrain interpretation; no generalized reliability or deployment claim is made.
Gold drafts test fixed decisions, while generated lines test a different distribution. Better fixed-probe acceptance alone is insufficient to demonstrate better complete conversation.

Final runtime subsequently removed the no-evidence extra newline. These raw measurements remain explicitly labeled V2; see the whole-chain audit's finalRuntimeOfflineDelta for byte-parity verification.
